Hi Marta — thanks for the note and the attachment. Below is the entrance criteria we verify before marking an environment "ready-for-commissioning." I tried to keep items evidence-oriented so you can hand us artifacts (screenshots, export CSVs, console links).

1) Network ownership & connectivity
   - Public egress IPs for outbound allowlist (static NATs preferred). Evidence: NAT IP list or IP range.
   - Ingress/NAT topology diagram (how traffic flows to/from Redwood endpoints).
   - Firewall rules: explicit list of allowed ports/hosts for control-plane and runtime. We check for: 443 outbound to s3/artefact hosts, 443 to telemetry endpoints, and 10250/10255 for health checks if using kubelet paths (where applicable).
   - VPN / Interconnect details (if private peering). Evidence: circuit IDs, BGP session status or peer IPs.

2) Access & credentials
   - Service account with least-privilege IAM role for deployment orchestration (ARN or service account name).
   - SSH/Bastion access plan: who is the day-zero operator (Redwood on-call vs customer SRE)? If Redwood needs a bastion jump host, provide an account and allowed source CIDR.
   - KMS / keywrap: KMS key ARN and admin contacts for key rotation requests.

3) Egress, data path & telemetry
   - Egress behavior: does customer NAT all traffic or are there split egress paths? We need to know for caching and KV prefix retrieval.
   - Telemetry endpoints: allowlist for tracing + metrics collectors and IPs/hostnames for our collector to push to.

4) Environment hardening & audit
   - Audit log retention policy and access method (where Redwood can request evidence for SOC-type audits).
   - Time sync/ntp checks and certificate trust anchors (for mTLS where used).

5) Smoke validation plan
   - Test endpoints/URLs we can call for a controlled smoke: tokenized API endpoint, health-check URL, and expected status codes.
   - Sample traffic profile: token sizes and QPS expectations for day-one testing.

Attachments I've included: "redwood-private-entrance-criteria-v1.pdf" and a blank "kiln-access-worksheet.csv" to capture items above.

Decisions we ask you to confirm in reply:
 - Which NAT IPs (or CIDR) will Redwood rely on for egress allowlisting?
 - Who will be the customer day-zero network contact for port/firewall coordination?
 - Do you expect us to SSH into a bastion or use a pre-provisioned deployment role/API key?

If you like, Ben or Karthik can join a 30-minute walkthrough to go through the checklist and diagram.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Soojin / Marta — quick follow-up from my side: for day-zero network verification we typically do the following checklist and assign an owner on the Redwood side. Suggestion below — please confirm if this works for Kiln.

Redwood day-zero verification checklist (operational):
 - Validate egress NAT IPs match submitted list (owner: Redwood network ops)
 - Confirm egress TLS handshake to telemetry/registry endpoints (owner: Redwood runtime eng)
 - Verify inbound/port reachability for any control-plane callbacks (owner: Customer NetOps; Redwood provides test endpoints)
 - Bastion access verified by SSH key injection test or ephemeral session (owner: Customer SRE unless customer requests Redwood access)

Proposed owners: Redwood network ops (Ben) -> nat/egress check & telemetry handshake; Customer SRE (Marta) -> firewall/open port confirmation & bastion validation. If Kiln can provide a pre-authenticated runbook or a test account that’s ideal.

One quick note on NACLs: if you have restrictive NACLs (stateful vs stateless) please include ephemeral port ranges used by our orchestration — we may need a short window to confirm connections during smoke tests.

Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
